candidate_classification_inputs: official identity, publisher, release or catalog identity, and vintage
statistical unit, target population, denominator construction, and observation period
advertised zero-incident, incident-count, loss, population, and geography fields
collection method, provenance, lineage, license, access, format, and size metadata

occurrences: Federal Statistical Office search results and historical enterprise-survey reports co-mingled quantitative findings with permitted survey identity and methodology metadata.
National Cyber Security Centre search results and report pages co-mingled report totals or category shares with permitted collection metadata.
Federal open-data search results co-mingled unrelated criminal-justice aggregates with catalog metadata.
incidental_value_quarantine.handling: No incident total, rate, share, loss, quantile, distribution, organization, or row value from those sections was transcribed, compared, summarized, persisted, or used in classification. Reading stopped at the metadata boundary.

candidates.title: IKT und E-Commerce in der Schweizer Wirtschaft, Unternehmensbefragung 2002
candidates.publisher: Swiss Federal Statistical Office; survey conducted by KOF Swiss Economic Institute
candidates.stable_release_identity: FSO asset 341200, 2003 publication describing the autumn 2002 enterprise survey

structural_evidence.period: enterprise survey conducted in autumn 2002 with stated reference periods in the instrument
structural_evidence.population_denominator: The methodology describes a representative enterprise survey and an enterprise sampling design.
structural_evidence.loss_support: No realized cyberincident-loss field is advertised.
structural_evidence.collection: Postal enterprise questionnaire conducted by KOF for the FSO
structural_evidence.format_and_size: Publisher-rendered historical report; record-level format and size not advertised

access_and_license.microdata_access_path: not advertised in the permitted metadata

blocking_gaps: The survey is an ICT and e-commerce instrument, not a documented organization-period cyberincident outcome collection.
Explicit zero-incident periods, incident counts, and realized-loss fields are not advertised.
Record-level access, license, current vintage, and overlap-exclusion terms are unresolved.

candidates.title: Business Census / Structural Business Statistics (STATENT): Enterprises

structural_evidence.population_denominator: Administrative-register-based full survey of business and economic structure, replacing the business census from 2011.
structural_evidence.zero_incident_support: not applicable; no cyberincident outcome is advertised

blocking_gaps: STATENT can describe the enterprise population but advertises no cyberincident, zero-event, incident-count, or realized-loss outcome fields.
No deterministic linkage to an independent incident collection is documented.
The permitted catalog record describes aggregate and geospatial resources, not governed organization-period research records.

candidates.title: NCSC voluntary cyberincident report collection and weekly statistics
candidates.stable_release_identity: NCSC weekly published classification series, available since mid-2020; metadata page dated 2022-04-01

structural_evidence.period: continuously collected and weekly classified publication
structural_evidence.population_denominator: No complete organization population or exposure denominator is advertised; reports may originate from private individuals or companies.
structural_evidence.incident_count_support: The administrative collection classifies submitted reports, but no organization-period count schema is advertised.
structural_evidence.loss_support: No realized monetary-loss field is advertised in the permitted collection metadata.
structural_evidence.collection: Voluntary reporting form; NCSC screening and main-category/subcategory classification
structural_evidence.record_access: Only aggregate interactive statistics are publicly described

blocking_gaps: Voluntary ascertainment has no organization-period denominator or zero-report organizations.
The statistical unit is a submitted report rather than an observed organization-period.
Reports from individuals and organizations are combined in the public collection description.
Potential overlap with public incident aggregators, the mandatory reporting lineage, IRIS, Advisen, VERIS, or DBIR is unresolved.

candidates.title: NCSC mandatory critical-infrastructure cyberattack report collection
candidates.stable_release_identity: Information Security Act and Cybersecurity Ordinance reporting collection effective 2025-04-01; metadata last modified 2026-05-19

structural_evidence.unit: reportable cyberattack affecting a covered critical-infrastructure operator
structural_evidence.period: initial report within 24 hours of discovery and completion within 14 days
structural_evidence.population_denominator: The law and ordinance define covered critical-infrastructure authorities and organizations, with exemptions, but the permitted public metadata does not enumerate a frozen exposed-organization denominator.
structural_evidence.zero_incident_support: absent; non-reporting organization-periods are not published as zero observations
structural_evidence.incident_count_support: Incident submissions are recorded, but no organization-period count export is advertised.
structural_evidence.loss_support: The public e-mail schema advertises operational impact severity fields but no realized monetary-loss amount, currency, or censoring field.
structural_evidence.collection: Cyber Security Hub or e-mail form; confidential, anonymized, categorized, and statistically recorded administrative reports
advertised_fields: availability, integrity, confidentiality, and operational impact

access_and_license.record_access_path: confidential administrative system; no public record-level access path advertised

blocking_gaps: No public frozen denominator, zero-incident organization-period rows, or organization-period count export is advertised.
The NCSC states there is no active supervision of compliance, so complete ascertainment cannot be inferred.
No realized monetary-loss field, record-level access, license, deidentification, retention, or missingness policy is advertised.
Potential overlap with voluntary NCSC reports and public incident aggregators is unresolved.

federal_open_data_catalog_finding.catalog_role: opendata.swiss publishes metadata references rather than hosting the source data itself.
federal_open_data_catalog_finding.result: Metadata-only exact-topic searches did not establish a distinct Swiss federal organization-period cybersecurity incident or realized-loss dataset beyond the four disclosed identities.

decision.result: No Swiss source discovered in the authorized funnel is structurally full-tier or magnitude-only, and none is acquisition-ready.
decision.remaining_gate: An independent, governed organization-period source must expose a target-population denominator, explicit zero-incident periods, incident counts, and realized-loss metadata with record-level access, license, deidentification, retention, missingness, and overlap controls.
decision.swiss_value: The NCSC mandatory collection supplies useful administrative incident-schema and covered-population context, while STATENT supplies enterprise-population context, but the public metadata does not document a lawful deterministic linkage or a combined analytical record set.
next_bounded_options: Retain the Swiss identities as aggregate context and run the previously identified narrow access-and-codebook qualification for the Statistics Canada 2017 lead and blocked UK enterprise-survey family.
If governed record-level access cannot be established, close OPT-014 at its completed descriptive coherence and negative data-feasibility scope without a universal impossibility claim.
